title: A Crossroads for the Democratic Party

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做DJ时，你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，你会把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In Georgia, two women have been locked in a close race for the Democratic nomination for governor.
sentences.zh: 在佐治亚州，两位女性正陷入一场激烈的民主党州长候选人提名之争。

sentences.en: What the election tells us about the future of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 这场选举揭示了民主党未来的走向。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, May 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月23日，星期三。

sentences.en: Jonathan, tell me about the first candidate in this race.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，跟我说说这场竞选中的第一位候选人。

sentences.en: Stacey Evans is a 40-year-old former state legislator.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·埃文斯是一位40岁的前州议员。

sentences.en: Growing up, I didn't know there was anything unusual about it.
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，我并不觉得这有什么不寻常的。

sentences.en: I just thought we moved a lot.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得我们搬家很频繁。

sentences.en: She grew up really modest means.
sentences.zh: 她是在非常拮据的环境中长大的。

sentences.en: I was born just outside of Ringgold, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我出生在佐治亚州灵戈尔德郊外。

sentences.en: My mom had me when she was 17.
sentences.zh: 我母亲17岁时生下了我。

sentences.en: And went to college on a scholarship.
sentences.zh: 后来我靠奖学金上了大学。

sentences.en: Jonathan Martin covers national politics for The Times.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·马丁负责《纽约时报》的全国政治报道。

sentences.en: I'd always assumed that I'd go to college, but I never thought about how I'd pay for it because we didn't have any money to do anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为我会上大学，但我从没想过该怎么付学费，因为我们根本没钱做那种事。

sentences.en: And is now running for governor.
sentences.zh: 而她现在正在竞选州长。

sentences.en: I remember what it was like to grow up in a family on the edge where you didn't know what the future might hold or even where you might live next year.
sentences.zh: 我记得在那种边缘家庭长大的感觉，你不知道未来会怎样，甚至不知道明年会住在哪里。

sentences.en: As governor, I'll never forget that.
sentences.zh: 作为州长，我永远不会忘记这一点。

sentences.en: What about the second candidate in this race?
sentences.zh: 那这场竞选中的第二位候选人呢？

sentences.en: Stacey Abrams, who is also a former state representative.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯，她也是一位前州众议员。

sentences.en: When I was 15, my parents were both admitted to Emory University to become Methodist ministers.
sentences.zh: 我15岁时，父母都被埃默里大学录取，去学习成为卫理公会牧师。

sentences.en: So they packed up our family, and we moved from Mississippi to Georgia.
sentences.zh: 于是他们收拾好家当，我们从密西西比州搬到了佐治亚州。

sentences.en: My parents had a car, a used car, that got us across Alabama and died a couple of months later.
sentences.zh: 我父母有一辆二手车，它载着我们穿过阿拉巴马州，几个月后就报废了。

sentences.en: 44 years old and a former small business owner, now running for governor.
sentences.zh: 她今年44岁，曾是一位小企业主，现在正在竞选州长。

sentences.en: I'm running for governor because I want to open the gates wide for everyone in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我竞选州长是因为我想为佐治亚州的每一个人敞开大门。

sentences.en: No one should feel that they don't belong in our Georgia.
sentences.zh: 没有人应该觉得他们不属于我们的佐治亚州。

sentences.en: That's my vision.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的愿景。

sentences.en: A vision of Georgia where everyone is welcome.
sentences.zh: 一个欢迎所有人的佐治亚州的愿景。

sentences.en: So two Stacys with somewhat similar backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 所以两位斯泰西的背景有些相似。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: With one key difference.
sentences.zh: 但有一个关键区别。

sentences.en: One's black, one's white.
sentences.zh: 一个是黑人，一个是白人。

sentences.en: I am deeply humbled by the possibility of being the first black woman ever elected to serve as governor in the United States.
sentences.zh: 如果能成为美国历史上第一位当选州长的黑人女性，我将深感荣幸。

sentences.en: And why is race so crucial?
sentences.zh: 为什么种族问题如此关键？

sentences.en: Well, because Georgia is a changing state.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为佐治亚州是一个正在变化的州。

sentences.en: This is certainly a conservative-looking state in the Deep South, but it's also home to very vibrant
sentences.zh: 这当然是一个看起来保守的深南部州，但它也是亚特兰大充满活力的

sentences.en: African-American community in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人社区的所在地。

sentences.en: And Atlanta has also become a kind of magnet for immigrants across the world.
sentences.zh: 而且亚特兰大也成为了世界各地移民的磁石。

sentences.en: So we're also curious, you know, is Georgia becoming more purple than red politically?
sentences.zh: 所以我们也很好奇，你知道，佐治亚州在政治上是否正在从红色变得更偏紫色？

sentences.en: I'm going to win this race by running a different kind of campaign, a people-powered campaign.
sentences.zh: 我将通过开展一种不同类型的竞选活动来赢得这场选举，一场由人民驱动的竞选。

sentences.en: So tell me more about Stacey Abrams' strategy here in her campaign for governor.
sentences.zh: 那么，请多告诉我一些斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯在州长竞选中的策略。

sentences.en: So her theory of the case is that conservative-leaning white voters, especially in the more rural parts of the state, aren't gettable.
sentences.zh: 她的理论是，倾向保守的白人选民，特别是在该州较偏远的农村地区，是争取不到的。

sentences.en: They're not coming back to the Democratic Party of their ancestors.
sentences.zh: 他们不会回到他们祖先支持的民主党了。

sentences.en: They're Republicans now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在是共和党人了。

sentences.en: And that it's time and money wasted trying to win them over when you can actually try to get more voters who are guaranteed to pull the lever for you to register and vote.
sentences.zh: 试图赢得他们是浪费时间和金钱，而你可以去争取那些肯定会为你投票的人，让他们注册并参与投票。

sentences.en: There are 800,000 people of color in the state of Georgia in 2014 who did not have the right to vote, not because they weren't eligible,
sentences.zh: 2014年，佐治亚州有80万有色人种没有投票权，不是因为他们没有资格，

sentences.en: but because no one had ever asked them to register.
sentences.zh: 而是因为从来没有人要求他们去注册。

sentences.en: That's the better investment.
sentences.zh: 那才是更好的投资。

sentences.en: Find immigrants, find Black non-voters, find recent 18- and 19-year-old kids who are now eligible to vote.
sentences.zh: 找到移民，找到不投票的黑人，找到刚满18岁和19岁、现在有资格投票的年轻人。

sentences.en: And so I took it upon myself to register all 800,000 people of color in the state of Georgia by 2024.
sentences.zh: 所以我承担起责任，要在2024年之前让佐治亚州所有80万有色人种完成注册。

sentences.en: Get them registered and turn them out on Election Day.
sentences.zh: 让他们注册，并在选举日出来投票。

sentences.en: So she's explicitly not trying to appeal to Trump voters, kind of white working class voters in Georgia, and pick them off.
sentences.zh: 所以她明确表示不打算争取特朗普的支持者，也就是佐治亚州的白人蓝领选民，并试图把他们拉过来。

sentences.en: Her strategy is to essentially stick with liberals, liberal ideologies, positions, and voters.
sentences.zh: 她的策略基本上是坚持自由派立场、意识形态和选民基础。

sentences.en: That's the gamble, that if you give those folks a reason to turn out, that they will show up in a midterm election when typically those constituencies don't vote.
sentences.zh: 这就是一场赌博，如果你给这些人一个投票的理由，他们就会在通常选民投票率不高的中期选举中现身。

sentences.en: That if you give them a reason by sort of doubling down on a more progressive ideology, that's the way to get them to the polls, and that's the way to win stay wide.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过坚持更进步的意识形态给他们一个理由，这就是让他们去投票站的方法，也是赢得全州胜利的方法。

sentences.en: There's the Georgia that was, a Georgia that was mired in discrimination and hatred, and that Georgia luckily is, I think, far behind us, but we still have a Georgia today
sentences.zh: 曾经有一个佐治亚州，一个深陷歧视和仇恨的佐治亚州，我认为那个佐治亚州幸运地已经离我们远去了，但我们今天仍然有一个佐治亚州

sentences.en: that grapples with some of that discrimination, some of that bigotry.
sentences.zh: 在与那种歧视和偏见作斗争。

sentences.en: You know, I was in Georgia last week.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我上周在佐治亚州。

sentences.en: I spent some time traveling with Stacey Abrams in seeing her talk to folks, and she is very clear.
sentences.zh: 我和斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯一起旅行了一段时间，看着她与人们交谈，她非常明确。

sentences.en: As she told me, she said, look, I'm not going to pander, and I am who I am.
sentences.zh: 正如她告诉我的，她说，看，我不会迎合任何人，我就是我。

sentences.en: But I'm running to be the governor of a new Georgia, of a Georgia that we all can see in this room, a Georgia that looks like this room.
sentences.zh: 但我竞选是为了成为一个新佐治亚州的州长，一个我们在这个房间里都能看到的佐治亚州，一个看起来像这个房间一样的佐治亚州。

sentences.en: And with your support on May 22nd, I will become the Democratic nominee for that new Georgia.
sentences.zh: 在5月22日得到你们的支持后，我将成为那个新佐治亚州的民主党提名人。

sentences.en: Are you with me?
sentences.zh: 你们支持我吗？

sentences.en: The other theory of the case is, don't necessarily reinvent the party to a Clinton-style, you know, centrist party, but do aggressively appeal to the Trump voters,
sentences.zh: 另一种理论是，不必非要将党重塑为克林顿式的中间派政党，而是要积极争取特朗普的支持者，

sentences.en: the working-class white voters who abandoned the party in 2016, and try to get them back while retaining the liberal core of the party.
sentences.zh: 那些在2016年抛弃了民主党的白人蓝领选民，在保留党内自由派核心的同时试图把他们拉回来。

sentences.en: And is that what Stacey Evans is doing?
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·埃文斯是在这样做吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: In the 18 years that I lived in Ringgold, we lived in 16 homes, most of them trailers, some of them empty lots now.
sentences.zh: 在我住在灵戈尔德的18年里，我们搬过16次家，大部分是拖车房，有些现在已经是空地了。

sentences.en: 16 homes, always one step ahead of a bill collector.
sentences.zh: 16个家，总是比收债人快一步。

sentences.en: We can get some of those folks back.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把其中一些人争取回来。

sentences.en: Not all of them, but you can get enough of them back, and when you combine that with some suburbanites who don't like Trump and the liberal core of the party,
sentences.zh: 不是全部，但你可以争取回足够多的人，当你把他们与一些不喜欢特朗普的郊区居民以及党内的自由派核心结合起来时，

sentences.en: that might get you to 50.1.
sentences.zh: 那可能会让你达到50.1%的得票率。

sentences.en: And I'm running for governor to be a champion for every family, for people who work hard and are trying to get ahead in an economy that leaves too many behind
sentences.zh: 我竞选州长是为了成为每个家庭的捍卫者，为了那些努力工作、试图在经济中取得进步，却被太多人抛在身后的人，

sentences.en: and seems more unfair in every way.
sentences.zh: 而且这种经济在各方面似乎都更加不公平。

sentences.en: And how is Evans approaching that strategically as a candidate in this primary?
sentences.zh: 作为初选候选人，埃文斯在战略上是如何处理这一点的？

sentences.en: What does it look like?
sentences.zh: 看起来是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, her case is that she can win back those kinds of voters in a way that Abrams can't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她的理由是她能以艾布拉姆斯无法做到的方式赢回那些选民。

sentences.en: My opponent, on the other hand, thinks you just focus on Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而我的对手认为你只需要专注于民主党人。

sentences.en: And if we just get all Democrats out, we'll win.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能让所有民主党人都出来投票，我们就会赢。

sentences.en: And in a state like Georgia, I don't think that's enough.
sentences.zh: 但在像佐治亚州这样的地方，我不认为这足够了。

sentences.en: I don't think the math adds up.
sentences.zh: 我不认为数学上行得通。

sentences.en: And I also just don't think it's healthy for democracy.
sentences.zh: 而且我也不认为这对民主健康有益。

sentences.en: And that the Abrams approach is going to backfire.
sentences.zh: 艾布拉姆斯的做法会适得其反。

sentences.en: She said that it's basically the equivalent of cowering in a corner with like-minded voters.
sentences.zh: 她说这基本上等同于和志同道合的选民躲在角落里。

sentences.en: Jonathan, is it fair to say that this is a campaign in which these two candidates' politics, their positions, are not all that different, but the way that they're representing
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，是否可以公平地说，这是一场两位候选人的政治立场并没有太大不同，但她们代表

sentences.en: those views and talking about them and campaigning and presenting to voters is very different?
sentences.zh: 这些观点、谈论它们、进行竞选以及向选民展示自己的方式却截然不同的竞选？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: There's not much difference in their actual ideology.
sentences.zh: 她们在实际意识形态上没有太大区别。

sentences.en: If you offered them, you know, eight, nine issues, they probably would be in agreement on all of them.
sentences.zh: 如果你给她们八九个议题，她们可能在所有议题上都会达成一致。

sentences.en: It's much more about their approach and their strategy and what they think is going to be effective in Georgia circa 2018.
sentences.zh: 这更多是关于她们的方法、策略，以及她们认为在2018年的佐治亚州什么才是有效的。

sentences.en: And yet they're becoming, despite these overlapping positions,
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管立场重叠，她们却正在成为

sentences.en: these symbolic polls of the Democratic Party, it sounds like, as we head into the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 民主党的象征性两极，听起来是这样，随着我们进入中期选举。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's why this race is so fascinating is because this debate echoes the broader national debate taking place among Democrats when it comes to how they take back
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这场竞选之所以如此引人入胜，是因为这场辩论呼应了民主党内部关于如何夺回

sentences.en: the presidency.
sentences.zh: 总统职位的更广泛的全国性辩论。

sentences.en: Do they do it by mobilizing more of their like-minded supporters or do they do it by trying to grab some of the Trump supporters and win back those who have strayed from the fold?
sentences.zh: 他们是通过动员更多志同道合的支持者来做到这一点，还是通过试图争取一些特朗普的支持者并赢回那些偏离党派的人来做到这一点？

sentences.en: That's the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Was the issue Hillary or was the issue her politics and Trump's politics?
sentences.zh: 问题出在希拉里身上，还是出在她的政治主张和特朗普的政治主张上？

sentences.en: Because if you believe that the problem was Hillary and that that's why there was a drop-off among younger and non-white voters, then you might not have an appetite
sentences.zh: 因为如果你认为问题出在希拉里身上，并且那是年轻选民和非白人选民流失的原因，那么你可能就没有兴趣

sentences.en: to try to win over the Trump voters again.
sentences.zh: 再次尝试赢得特朗普的支持者了。

sentences.en: But the Abrams-Evans divide or lack of it suggests that perhaps the midterms are becoming more about strategy and packaging than perhaps substance and policy.
sentences.zh: 但艾布拉姆斯与埃文斯之间的分歧（或缺乏分歧）表明，中期选举可能正变得更关乎策略和包装，而非实质和政策。

sentences.en: There's no question about it that the Democratic Party has moved to the left.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，民主党已经向左转了。

sentences.en: There's not much of a centrist wing left in the party and it is much more now about the presentation and packaging than it is about the issue set, right?
sentences.zh: 党内几乎没有中间派了，现在更多的是关于展示和包装，而不是议题设置，对吧？

sentences.en: There's not a lot of Democrats left who are going to take the NRA line or oppose abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 剩下的民主党人中，没几个会接受全国步枪协会（NRA）的路线或反对堕胎权了。

sentences.en: And let me just make one more point.
sentences.zh: 让我再补充一点。

sentences.en: Democrats are finding a lot of success in nominating women in this year's primaries and there's no question that the energy behind the kind of anti-Trump movement has been led
sentences.zh: 民主党在今年的初选中提名女性方面取得了很大成功，毫无疑问，反特朗普运动背后的能量一直是由

sentences.en: by women.
sentences.zh: 女性领导的。

sentences.en: If you talk to Democrats privately though, they recognize that this can't be the year of the white woman, right?
sentences.zh: 不过，如果你私下与民主党人交谈，他们会意识到这不能成为“白人女性之年”，对吧？

sentences.en: That a party that so heavily relies on the votes of black women can't just be defined by, you know, white women in pussy hats.
sentences.zh: 一个如此严重依赖黑人女性选票的政党，不能仅仅被戴着猫耳帽的白人女性所定义。

sentences.en: That it's got to be a broader cross-section of females representing their party in office.
sentences.zh: 必须有更广泛的女性群体代表她们的政党担任公职。

sentences.en: There's got to be some success stories from women of color.
sentences.zh: 必须有一些有色人种女性的成功故事。

sentences.en: Hello, this is Hillary Clinton asking you to vote for my friend,
sentences.zh: 你好，我是希拉里·克林顿，请在这个周二投票支持我的朋友，

sentences.en: Stacey Abrams for governor of Georgia this Tuesday,
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯竞选佐治亚州州长，

sentences.en: May 22nd.
Abrams, with an A, is the first black woman to serve as House Democratic leader, a small business innovator.
sentences.zh: 艾布拉姆斯（Abrams，以A开头），是第一位担任众议院民主党领袖的黑人女性，也是一位小企业创新者。

sentences.en: Democrats rely on African-American votes and particularly black women for their votes and it's difficult for Democrats to keep doing that and not putting forward black women
sentences.zh: 民主党依赖非裔美国人的选票，特别是黑人女性的选票，如果民主党继续这样做却不推举黑人女性

sentences.en: as candidates.
sentences.zh: 作为候选人，这很困难。

sentences.en: They can't just be a loyal constituency for the party when it comes to election day but then not actually be nominated and win elections.
sentences.zh: 她们不能仅仅在选举日成为党内忠诚的选民基础，却不能真正获得提名并赢得选举。

sentences.en: Zero black women have been elected governor in the history of the country.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家的历史上，还没有黑人女性当选过州长。

sentences.en: Two black women have been elected to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 只有两位黑人女性当选过美国

sentences.en: Senate.
sentences.zh: 参议员。

sentences.en: There's one black woman there, Kamala Harris, right now.
sentences.zh: 现在那里只有一位黑人女性，卡玛拉·哈里斯。
